raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #44884; this PR contains only the exact comparison-rank lookup follow-up.

## Motivation

The fused greedy-verification logits reduction still computes FP32 softcap for every vocabulary element. BF16 has only 65,536 bit patterns, so build exact comparison ranks through the existing native FP32 softcap once and reduce those ranks instead. This preserves transformed equality classes, including softcap saturation, signed zero, and NaNs. Weights, BF16 logits, and the head GEMM remain unchanged.

## Modifications

- Extend the XPU reduction with an optional immutable 256 KB comparison table and unsigned-rank/first-index reductions.
- Keep the table in a nonpersistent LogitsProcessor buffer, keyed by generation device and softcap. Construct it during eager warmup; unmatched first capture or compile keeps the existing tanh reduction.
- Carry the immutable table reference with deferred logits through graph replay. Slice token rows without slicing the table. Current-request eligibility and the ordinary-logits fallback remain unchanged.

The table records exact FP32 output ordering and equality for the actual native softcap operation; it does not approximate or change model precision. Scope remains no-gather Gemma4 BF16 FrozenKV target verification, validated at TP1.

## Accuracy Tests

- Exhaustive native FP32 softcap order/equality proof across all 65,536 BF16 bit patterns for softcap None, zero, and 30; device lookup checked for every pattern.
- Six XPU kernel tests passed, including signed zero, saturation ties, first NaN/global index, chunk boundaries, public lazy dispatch, Meta shapes, and graph replay with changed inputs.
- Two real LogitsProcessor lifetime/capture tests passed, covering separate owners, cap changes, nonpersistent state, immutable captured references, and no table construction inside first capture.
- 75 CPU namespace/policy tests and 15 subtests passed. Rank-aware Meta smoke and pre-commit passed.
- Fifteen controlled same-GPU serving cases matched the parent exactly, including returned token logprobs and repetition-penalty/bias/min-new-token fallbacks.
- Official GSM8K200, temperature 0, seed 42, eight threads: parent 159/200 (79.5%), candidate 164/200 (82.0%), zero errors and two truncations each. Earlier parent serving scored 165/200; these are compatibility results, with no quality-improvement claim.
- Candidate official GSM8K200 temperature 1: 165/200 (82.5%), zero errors, two truncations. This uses the ordinary-logits fallback, not the changed greedy reduction.

Exact operator and controlled-serving parity do not establish arbitrary batch-independent model bitwise equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same-GPU ABBA versus parent 7aba: Gemma4 E2B BF16, TP1, MTP steps 3/top-k 1/draft tokens 4, full graph backend; actual target-verify capture sizes end at 48, overlap disabled, page size 64, max running 64, max total tokens 32768, context 8192, static memory fraction 0.70. Each server switch warmed 128 requests at c32 with 256 output tokens. Timing uses seed 42 and 256 outputs, 64 requests at c1 and 128 at c8/c32. All 12 runs completed without errors, with identical input/output token counts.

Mean TPOT, ms, control/candidate/candidate/control:

| Concurrency | Control A | Candidate A | Candidate B | Control B | Lower time vs mean controls | Lower time vs final control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 |4.129629|4.120205|4.115793|4.093881|-0.152%|-0.589%|
| 8 |6.017597|5.979372|5.986314|5.960932|0.107%|-0.368%|
| 32 |10.882142|10.804637|10.778815|10.925135|1.026%|1.221%|

C1/c8 are near flat and slightly slower versus final controls. At c32, both candidate repeats beat both controls; final control was 0.395% slower than initial, and candidate mean was 0.831% lower than initial control. On 55/128 requests with identical texts across all four c32 runs, mean streaming-time improvement was 1.014%. Controls differed on 38/128 texts; candidates differed on 48/128. This subset does not remove between-run drift.

Additional bounded c64 ABBA uses 256 requests/run with 256 output tokens, a deterministic repeated copy of the 200 canonical prompts, and 256-request c64 warmup per server switch:

| Concurrency | Control A | Candidate A | Candidate B | Control B | Lower time vs mean controls | Lower time vs final control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 |20.931916|20.349956|20.459503|20.564288|1.655%|0.776%|

Control improved 1.756% between repeats, so the final-control comparison is conservative. Both candidate repeats beat final control. The 109/256 identical-text subset improved 1.753% in mean streaming time; controls differed on 92/256 texts and candidates on 107/256. These figures retain between-run drift limitations.

C64 is mixed eager/captured execution: startup logs resolve target-verify capture sizes through 48, every logged above 48-request decode batch used eager execution, and smaller decode batches also used captured execution. All four runs succeeded without errors and had identical input/output token counts.

A real c32 serving trace contains 16 rank partial/final reductions, confirming actual dispatch. Profile timing alone is not an end-to-end gain measurement.

Bounded eager head-plus-finalization microbenchmark, four rotating original BF16 weight banks (3.2 GB), compared to the parent tanh reduction:

| Rows | Parent us | Rank-table us | Lower time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 1371.28 | 1370.04 | 0.09% |
| 32 | 1524.96 | 1500.50 | 1.60% |
| 128 | 1971.09 | 1822.13 | 7.56% |
| 256 | 2576.16 | 2217.53 | 13.92% |

These are microbenchmarks, not serving gains. Fixed 4096 chunks use 16 B shared memory and report zero spill bytes; the table adds 256 KB model-owned GPU storage and indexed read traffic. An 8192-chunk candidate offered no consistent improvement. No achieved-occupancy claim is inferred from compiler resource reports.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add kernel and runtime lifetime tests.
- [x] Document exact semantics, state ownership, capture fallback, and scope.
- [x] Finish and archive paired serving benchmarks and official quality results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

-def softcap_argmax(logits, softcap=None, sanitize=False):
+@triton.jit
+def _rank(value, Table):
+    bits = value.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.int32)
+    return tl.load(Table + bits).to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _rank_partial(
+    X,
+    Table,
+    Ranks,
+    Indices,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNKS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    col = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    valid = col < N
+    value = tl.load(X + row * STRIDE + col, valid, other=0)
+    ranks = _rank(value, Table)
+    best = tl.max(tl.where(valid, ranks, 0), 0)
+    index = tl.min(tl.where(valid & (ranks == best), col, 2147483647), 0)
+    tl.store(Ranks + row * CHUNKS + tl.program_id(1), best.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True))
+    tl.store(Indices + row * CHUNKS + tl.program_id(1), index)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _rank_finish(Ranks, Indices, Out, CHUNKS: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    col = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    valid = col < CHUNKS
+    ranks = tl.load(Ranks + row * CHUNKS + col, valid, other=0).to(
+        tl.uint32, bitcast=True
+    )
+    ids = tl.load(Indices + row * CHUNKS + col, valid, other=2147483647)
+    best = tl.max(tl.where(valid, ranks, 0), 0)
+    result = tl.min(tl.where(valid & (ranks == best), ids, 2147483647), 0)
+    tl.store(Out + row, result)
+
+
+def softcap_argmax(logits, softcap=None, sanitize=False, comparison_ranks=None):
     """Reduce BF16 logits after FP32 softcap, retaining first-token ties/NaNs."""
     if logits.ndim != 2 or logits.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
         raise ValueError("softcap_argmax expects rank-two BF16 logits")
     if logits.stride(1) != 1 or logits.shape[1] == 0:
         raise ValueError("softcap_argmax expects nonempty contiguous vocabulary rows")
+    if comparison_ranks is not None:
+        if sanitize:
+            raise ValueError("comparison ranks support unsanitized logits only")
+        if (
+            comparison_ranks.dtype != torch.int32
+            or comparison_ranks.shape != (65536,)
+            or not comparison_ranks.is_contiguous()
+            or comparison_ranks.device != logits.device
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "comparison ranks must be contiguous int32[65536] on the logits device"
+            )
     if logits.device.type == "meta":
         return torch.empty((logits.shape[0],), device=logits.device, dtype=torch.int64)
     if logits.device.type != "xpu":
         raise ValueError("softcap_argmax requires XPU")
+    if comparison_ranks is not None:
+        m, n = logits.shape
+        chunks = triton.cdiv(n, 4096)
+        ranks = torch.empty((m, chunks), device=logits.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+        indices = torch.empty_like(ranks)
+        out = torch.empty((m,), device=logits.device, dtype=torch.int64)
+        _rank_partial[(m, chunks)](
+            logits,
+            comparison_ranks,
+            ranks,
+            indices,
+            n,
+            logits.stride(0),
+            chunks,
+            4096,
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+        _rank_finish[(m,)](
+            ranks, indices, out, chunks, triton.next_power_of_2(chunks), num_warps=4
+        )
+        return out

+def make_verify_softcap_ranks(device, softcap):
+    """Build an immutable comparison table using the actual device softcap.
+
+    This is model-owned warmup data, not a process-global cache. The table
+    represents exact FP32 output ordering/equality for all BF16 bit patterns;
+    it does not approximate or change logits. Unsanitized NaNs sort first.
+    """
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.activation.softcap import softcap_inplace_logits

+    ranks = torch.where(values == 0, 0x80000000, ranks)

+            .to(torch.int16)

+                for (left, a), (right, b) in zip(pairs, pairs[1:]):
+                    equal = (math.isnan(left) and math.isnan(right)) or left == right

+                )

+        table = make_verify_softcap_ranks(
+            torch.device("xpu", torch.xpu.current_device()), 30.0
+        )

+"""Model-owned exact softcap table lifetime across warmup and capture."""
+
+import unittest
+from dataclasses import replace
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.logits_processor import LogitsProcessor, LogitsProcessorOutput
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=20, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-xpu")
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.xpu.is_available(), "requires XPU")
+class TestDeferredVerifyRanks(CustomTestCase):
+    def processor(self, cap=30.0):
+        with get_context().override_server_args(
+            model_path="dummy", device="xpu", tp_size=1
+        ):
+            return LogitsProcessor(
+                SimpleNamespace(vocab_size=262144, final_logit_softcapping=cap),
+                defer_xpu_verify_logits=True,
+            )
+
+    def test_owner_lifetime_softcap_changes_and_graph_output(self):
+        processor = self.processor()
+        device = torch.device("xpu", torch.xpu.current_device())
+        table = processor._get_verify_softcap_ranks(device)
+        self.assertIs(processor._get_verify_softcap_ranks(device), table)
+        self.assertNotIn("_verify_softcap_ranks", processor.state_dict())
+        other = self.processor()
+        self.assertIsNone(other._verify_softcap_ranks)
+        self.assertIsNot(other._get_verify_softcap_ranks(device), table)
+        raw = torch.empty(8, 262144, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        output = LogitsProcessorOutput(
+            next_token_logits=None,
+            deferred_verify_logits=raw,
+            deferred_verify_softcap=30.0,
+            deferred_verify_comparison_ranks=table,
+        )
+        sliced = replace(output, deferred_verify_logits=raw[:3])
+        self.assertEqual(sliced.deferred_verify_logits.shape[0], 3)
+        self.assertIs(sliced.deferred_verify_comparison_ranks, table)
+        processor.final_logit_softcapping = None
+        replacement = processor._get_verify_softcap_ranks(device)
+        self.assertIsNot(replacement, table)
+        self.assertFalse(torch.equal(replacement, table))
+        # Existing captured output keeps its original cap/table even if the
+        # owner prepares another configuration later.
+        self.assertIs(output.deferred_verify_comparison_ranks, table)
+        self.assertEqual(output.deferred_verify_softcap, 30.0)
+
+    def test_first_capture_does_not_construct_persistent_table(self):
+        processor = self.processor()

+        marker = torch.zeros(1, device=device)
+        graph = torch.xpu.XPUGraph()
+        with torch.xpu.graph(graph):
+            self.assertIsNone(processor._get_verify_softcap_ranks(device))
+            marker.add_(1)
+        self.assertIsNone(processor._verify_softcap_ranks)
+        table = processor._get_verify_softcap_ranks(device)
+        self.assertEqual(table.shape, (65536,))
+        other_graph = torch.xpu.XPUGraph()
+        with torch.xpu.graph(other_graph):
+            self.assertIs(processor._get_verify_softcap_ranks(device), table)
+            marker.add_(1)

+        third_graph = torch.xpu.XPUGraph()
+        with torch.xpu.graph(third_graph):
